newsitem.title: USA: MBNA sees growth through acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: MBNA sees growth through acquisitions.

text.p: MBNA America Bank N.A. vice chairman and chief admnistrative officer Lance Weaver said one of the ways the bank will continue to grow is by acquiring smaller competitors.
"We think there's going to be a great deal of merger and consolidation over the next years. We're going to be one of the acquirors, not one of the acquirees," Weaver said Thursday.

He cited the recent example of the January merger of First USA and Banc One. But Weaver told Reuters that any MBNA acquisitions would likely be small credit card operations that are beginning to find it too costly to compete in a consolidating industry.
"At some point credit card entities that are smaller may come knocking on our door," Weaver said. He would not comment on whether any candidates were now being considered.
Weaver said the credit card industry still had good growth potential.

"Credit cards account for only nine percent of all retail sales. 91 percent of sales are in cash. I think there's a lot of opportunity to go into that 91 percent and capture a lot of those transactions," Weaver said.
MBNA recently opened an insurance business and plans to expand its consumer finance loans. The bank currently has one million non-credit card customers, according to Weaver.

Wilmington-based MBNA has offices in 11 states and the UK, with plans for opening facilities in Maryland by spring. Weaver said in 1998 there will be a western regional headquarters in Arizona and that MBNA "intends to go into Canada" and possibly Dublin, Ireland.
"The purpose of our national expansion is to get closer to our customers," Weaver said, adding that MBNA has 24 million customers worldwide.
According to bank spokesman Peter Frank, MBNA has increased its managed loans from $9.9 billion at year end 1992 to $38.6 billion at the end of 1996.
